pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: Draw the three packages in your notes service and the arrows between them. Which package declares the `Store` interface, and why that one rather than `memstore`?
expected_points: api imports note; memstore imports note; nothing imports api or memstore except main
the domain sits at the center and depends on nobody — no net/http import in note
the interface is declared by the consumer (note), so storage implements the domain's vocabulary
swapping storage (e.g. SQLite later) touches one new implementation plus the wiring in main, not note or api

questions.prompt: A client posts `{"title":"   "}`. Walk through what happens from the request body to the response body, and say what the client sees.
expected_points: decode into a Draft; a decode failure would itself be a 400 (invalid JSON), never a panic
trim before validating, so a whitespace-only title fails the required check
validation produces data — a field name to message map — not prose
the response is 400 with a fields map like {"title": "required"} the client can act on
limits count runes (utf8.RuneCountInString), not bytes

questions.prompt: Product wants duplicate titles rejected with 409 Conflict. What do you add, and where? Then explain what stops that answer from being 'edit every handler'.
expected_points: a sentinel like note.ErrConflict defined in the domain next to ErrNotFound
one new case in respondError — the single function where an error meets a status code
errors.Is for sentinels, errors.As for typed errors like ValidationError
handlers only ever hand the error to respondError, so translation cannot drift between them

questions.prompt: Give the status code and body shape your service returns for POST /notes (valid), GET /notes (empty), and DELETE /notes/{id} (existing). Why is each one what it is?
expected_points: 201 Created with {"data": {…}} including the server-assigned id
200 with exactly {"data":[]} — an empty list must encode as [], never null, so return a non-nil slice
204 No Content with no body at all
Content-Type: application/json set before writing; success under data, failure under error, so clients branch on which key exists

questions.prompt: `note/service_test.go` imports no httptest at all. What made that possible, and what would you lose if the trimming and validation rules lived in the handler instead?
expected_points: the rules never needed HTTP, so they live below the edge and are testable as plain function calls
a handler's job is only decode, delegate, encode — past ~10 lines it is doing a lower layer's job
rules in handlers would be reachable only through requests: slower, noisier tests that point at a status code instead of the broken rule
the rules would also be unreachable from any other entry point (CLI, queue consumer, gRPC)

questions.prompt: Your store fails with `dial tcp 10.0.0.7:5432: connection refused`. What does the client get, what does the operator get, and why the difference?
expected_points: the client gets 500 with exactly {"error": {"message": "internal error"}}
the real error goes to slog on the server, structured, so operators can debug
raw error text leaks topology and internals to an attacker and confuses users who cannot act on it
the client cannot fix a 500 anyway — that is what separates it from the 400 family

questions.prompt: You build a `ValidationError{}`, find no problems, and return it. Every valid request now 400s. Explain the bug.
expected_points: an error interface holding a non-nil concrete value is non-nil even when the map is empty
the caller's err != nil is true, so the handler renders a validation failure
the fix is to check len() and return a literal nil when there is nothing wrong
same typed-nil trap as returning a nil *T as an error interface
